focus: Frontier node F-2-006 (depth 2, scope OpenBot-main/api/openapi/memory.yaml, .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/bots-schedule): How does an OpenBot memory source sync clock (nextSyncAt, syncStatus) map onto our cron and queue triggers?
noveltyJustification: 13 of 16 findings are new external evidence from the trigger model, the installer and the queue; 3 are new mapping inferences that reuse the existing cron and request paths.
keyQuestions: How do the reference repos build bot memory (per-bot and shared) and skills (written, recorded from a demonstration, proposed from use), and how would those map onto Skilled skills and the spec-kit?
answeredQuestions: How does an OpenBot memory source sync clock (nextSyncAt, syncStatus) map onto our cron and queue triggers?
ruledOut: A fifth trigger kind for memory sync
Storing nextSyncAt as a computed timestamp
A separate sync scheduler beside the drain job

label: OpenBot's MemorySource carries a sync clock: syncStatus is an extensible enum idle | running | succeeded | error, syncError is why the last sync failed in a sentence for the person, lastSyncAt is a nullable date-time and nextSyncAt is a non-nullable date-time.
The example cadence is fifteen minutes: lastSyncAt 2026-11-14T08:45:00Z beside nextSyncAt 2026-11-14T09:00:00Z.

The runtime has exactly four trigger kinds (cron with an expression, queue with a name, git-hook, manual) and validates a trigger block against its kind's allowed keys, refusing an unknown key rather than ignoring it.
A cron expression becomes launchd calendar dictionaries or an interval, and every cron string either fires exactly as cron would or is refused with a named invariant id.
The runtime never computes a next fire time: NEXT_FIRE_UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN because no launchd surface reports it.
A queued request has exactly two kinds, run and resume, and carries a free-form source string plus an origin naming who or what produced it.
The queue's retry policy is already bounded: RETRY_BOUND is 3, and the drain job has a 60-second throttle with a 300-second backoff base doubling to a 3600-second cap.
bots schedule install drain installs the repository's queue-drain job, and a first install is always held disabled until bots enable.
A scheduled run uses only the BOT.md and bots/config.json an operator approved, and is refused as definition-drifted after either file changes.
A memory source sync is a cron trigger, not a new trigger kind: the source's cadence is the cron expression and the sync is a run request with source memory-sync and origin the source id.
nextSyncAt should not be stored: the runtime already refuses to predict a next fire, so the field becomes a display derivation from the source's cron expression or drops out of the record.
syncStatus is fully derivable and should not be stored: idle is no request in the queue for that source, running is a claimed request, and succeeded or error is the last run record's exit.
syncError maps onto the run record's failure reason, which the delivery message already renders as a sentence for the person.
lastSyncAt maps onto the last run record's dispatch time, which the status index already stores per run.
A failed sync needs no new retry policy: the queue's RETRY_BOUND of 3 and the drain job's 60-second throttle with 300-to-3600-second backoff already bound it.
The smallest change is one new source string and one cron expression per source, with no new trigger kind, no new store and no new retry path.

direction: A fifth trigger kind for memory sync
reason: The four kinds already cover a timed read-in, and a new kind needs its own validation, install path and drift rule.

direction: Store nextSyncAt as a computed timestamp
reason: The runtime deliberately reports UNKNOWN for a next fire because no launchd surface reports one, so a stored value would be a guess that goes stale.
All four values are already readable from the queue and the last run record, so a stored copy could disagree with them.

direction: A separate sync scheduler beside the drain job
reason: The drain job already runs on a throttle with backoff and already claims requests from the inbox.
